comment: Comedian essay series. Consumed by scripts/publish-essays.js (workflow: publish-essays.yml) and scripts/generate-essay-graphics.js (workflow: essay-promo.yml). Each entry is one WP post in the comedy-advice category, indexed (no ch_noindex). schedule_gmt=null publishes immediately; a future ISO date creates a scheduled ('future') post; a past date publishes immediately. pull_quotes feed the Puppeteer quote cards (3 per essay, recyclable); ig_caption is the ready-to-post Instagram caption. House style: no em dashes anywhere in copy (both scripts enforce this). Images are Unsplash (free license, no attribution required).

essays.excerpt: You're funny live. Your clips die at 200 views. The problem isn't the algorithm, it's the first two seconds. How to cut stand-up clips that strangers actually watch.
essays.image_alt: Comedy club stage under colored lights with a crowd raising phones
pull_quotes: The algorithm never saw your comedy. It saw you adjusting the mic stand.
A set is built for a room. A clip is built for a thumb.
The clip is not a ranking of your material. It's an ad for it.
essays.ig_caption:
Your clip didn't flop because the algorithm hates you. It flopped in the first 2 seconds.

New on the blog: how to cut a stand-up clip strangers actually watch. Why you open AT the laugh, why the caption is the real setup, and why your best joke might be your worst clip.

Link in bio.

essays.excerpt: The green room says crowd work clips are ruining stand-up. The box office says they're filling it. Why crowd work is the free ad campaign for your written hour.
essays.image_alt: Audience seated in a dark showroom watching a live performance
pull_quotes: Your closer is the product. Crowd work is the commercial.
Post a hundred crowd work clips and your written hour is untouched. Post your closer and it's gone.
Would you rather be right about the trend or in front of it?
essays.ig_caption:
Hot take from the blog: crowd work clips aren't ruining stand-up. They're the free ad campaign filling the rooms your written hour plays to.

Unburnable content, 2-second proof, and the funnel nobody in the green room wants to admit works. Full argument at the link in bio.

essays.excerpt: We list every comedy show in Houston, so we see who fills the big rooms. None of them did it with festival laurels. What replaced the credit system, and what to do about it.
essays.image_alt: Packed arena crowd facing a bright stage
pull_quotes: 'As seen on' answers a question no ticket buyer is asking.
Strangers with laurels lose to known quantities at every box office in America.
The audience is the only gatekeeper left, and they have never once checked a resume.
essays.ig_caption:
You got the credit. The rooms stayed the same size.

We list every comedy show in Houston, so we see who actually fills the big rooms. None of them did it with laurels. What replaced the credit system, on the blog.

essays.excerpt: Stage time makes you good. It has never made anyone known. The open mic math nobody wants to do, and the second job every working comic now has.
essays.image_alt: Close-up of a microphone on a dark stage
pull_quotes: Stage time makes you good. Stage time has never once made anyone known.
A thousand more sets at the same eight mics rounds you into a beautifully polished secret.
Getting good and getting seen are two different jobs. You've only been showing up to one.
essays.ig_caption:
1,000 sets. Still opening.

The problem was never your work ethic. You're working one job and careers now take two. The open mic math nobody wants to do, on the blog. Link in bio.

(Every Houston mic is on the site, updated daily.)

essays.excerpt: 41 likes on the flyer, 38 from comics, 9 paid at the door. Why show promotion stays trapped inside the scene, and how to sell the night instead of the lineup.
essays.image_alt: Group of friends laughing together at a table
pull_quotes: You can't sell tickets to the cast.
She isn't buying a comedian. She's buying a night.
Your flyer is a cast list for a play she's never heard of.
essays.ig_caption:
41 likes on the flyer. 38 were comics. 9 paid.

If your show promo only reaches the scene, you're marketing to people who get in free. How to sell the NIGHT instead of the lineup, for producers and comics, on the blog.

essays.excerpt: 8,000 followers, 19 in the room. Followers are rented; an email list is owned. The stool-sign system that turns full rooms into an audience you keep.
essays.image_alt: Phone screen showing a mail app icon with unread badge
pull_quotes: Fifty people who paid once will outdraw five thousand who double-tapped.
Followers are prospects. The list is the audience.
Every show without a signup is an audience you built and handed back to the algorithm.
essays.ig_caption:
8,000 followers. 19 in the room.

The gap between your follower count and your folding chairs has a fix. It's boring and it works: the stool sign. Full system on the blog, 10 minutes to set up, free forever.
